did_you_know.text: Did you know? Psalm 132 opens with a plea to remember David’s hardships and efforts, highlighting his concern for a fitting place to worship the Lord.
Did you know? David is described as one who made a vow and swore an oath to the Lord, to the “Mighty One of Jacob”—a title for the Lord that appears in this psalm.
Did you know? David emphasizes that he will not enter his house or lie on his bed, expressing his determination not to rest until he finds a place for the Lord.
Did you know? David’s goal is expressed as finding a place for the Lord and for the “dwelling places” of the Mighty One of Jacob—an expression emphasizing the holiness of the place where God dwells.
Did you know? The psalmist mentions two locations associated with finding a place for the Lord: Ephrathah and the fields of Jaar, though the verse itself does not specify their exact identification.
Did you know? The call, “Arise, Lord, and come to your resting place,” is paired with a reference to the “ark of your might,” linking the Lord’s rest with the presence of the ark.
Did you know? God’s promise to David is that the fruit of his body will sit on his throne, presented as a divine oath that will not be revoked.
Did you know? The continuation of the dynasty depends on David’s sons keeping the Lord’s covenant and testimonies; the psalm therefore presents both a promise and a responsibility.
Did you know? Zion is described as the place the Lord chose and desired as his dwelling, not merely as a place chosen by human beings.
Did you know? Zion’s blessing also includes social concern: the Lord promises to bless its provisions and satisfy its poor with bread.
